Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Alexander von Humboldt (author, Wikidata Q6694), died 1859; Hermann Hauff (translator, Wikidata Q1611417), died 1865. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Humboldt, Alexander von, 1769-1859; Hauff, Hermann, 1800-1865 [Translator]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: Gesammelte Werke, Stuttgart J.G. Cotta, 1889, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/gesammeltewerke04humb. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 58%, 100%, 70% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Hermann Hauff, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
